articles.title: Previsão do tempo Paraíba: calor de 38°C no feriado de Aparecida | G1
articles.standfirst: De acordo com dados do Climatempo, a previsão é que o fim de semana seja predominantemente ensolarado, sem muitos registros de chuvas.
articles.summary: O feriado de Nossa Senhora Aparecida terá sol predominante e calor intenso em todo o estado, com máximas variando entre 30°C e 38°C segundo o Climatempo.
articles.body:
A previsão do tempo para este sábado (10), domingo (11) e segunda-feira (12), feriadão de Nossa Senhora Aparecida e Dia das Crianças, indica temperaturas entre 20°C e 38°C em diferentes municípios da Paraíba. Segundo o Climatempo, a previsão é de pouca chuva no estado.

Em João Pessoa , as temperaturas devem variar entre 23°C e 32°C no sábado (10). No domingo (11), a mínima será de 23°C, e a máxima pode chegar a 33°C. Na segunda-feira (12), os termômetros devem marcar entre 25°C e 29°C. A previsão é de sol na maior parte do tempo, com possibilidade de chuva pela manhã e à noite nos três dias.

Em Campina Grande , as temperaturas devem variar entre 20°C e 31°C no sábado (10) e na segunda-feira (12). No domingo (11), aniversário de 162 anos da cidade, a mínima será de 20°C, e a máxima pode chegar a 30°C. Segundo o Climatempo, o céu deve ficar parcialmente nublado, sem previsão de chuva nos três dias.

No Sertão paraibano, Patos deve registrar temperaturas entre 23°C e 38°C no sábado (10). No domingo (11), os termômetros devem marcar entre 23°C e 37°C. Já na segunda-feira (12), a variação prevista é de 24°C a 38°C. Segundo a previsão, o tempo deve ficar ensolarado, sem chuva nos três dias.

Em Pombal , também no Sertão, as temperaturas devem variar entre 25°C e 37°C no sábado (10). No domingo (11) e na segunda-feira (12), a mínima prevista é de 24°C. A máxima deve permanecer em 37°C nos três dias. Assim como em Patos, a previsão é de sol e ausência de chuva durante o feriadão.

Em Cabaceiras , no Cariri paraibano, as temperaturas devem variar entre 21°C e 33°C no sábado (10). No domingo (11), a mínima pode cair para 20°C, enquanto a máxima deve permanecer em 33°C. Na segunda-feira (12), a previsão é de temperaturas entre 21°C e 33°C. O céu deve ficar nublado nos três dias, sem previsão de chuva.

No Brejo, na cidade de Bananeiras , as temperaturas devem variar entre 21°C e 31°C no sábado (10). No domingo (11), a mínima prevista é de 22°C, e a máxima, de 30°C. Na segunda-feira (12), os termômetros devem voltar a marcar entre 21°C e 31°C.

Segundo o Climatempo, há previsão de chuva em diferentes períodos do feriadão em Bananeiras. No sábado (10), o dia deve ser ensolarado, com possibilidade de chuva pela manhã. No domingo (11), o sol deve predominar, mas podem ocorrer pancadas rápidas ao longo do dia. Na segunda-feira (12), a previsão é de chuva à noite.

articles.title: Telemedicina em Macapá: app oferece consultas e receitas digitais | G1
articles.standfirst: Plataforma 'Saúde da Gente' reúne mais de 35 especialidades médicas. UBS Macapaba inaugurou sala para orientar pacientes com dificuldades no uso da tecnologia.
articles.summary: O aplicativo Saúde da Gente disponibiliza telemedicina em Macapá com 35 especialidades e suporte presencial na UBS Macapaba para pacientes com dificuldades tecnológicas.
articles.body:
Aplicativo 'Saúde da gente', de telemedicina. — Foto: Isadora Pereira/g1

Um aplicativo de telemedicina passou a integrar a rede pública de saúde de Macapá com a oferta de consultas médicas gratuitas por videochamada em mais de 35 especialidades .

Chamada de Saúde da Gente, a plataforma permite agendamentos remotos, emissão de receitas digitais e acompanhamento de pacientes com doenças crônicas, como hipertensão e diabetes.

O acesso ao serviço exige o download do aplicativo em smartphones e o preenchimento de um cadastro inicial.

As consultas ocorrem diretamente pela ferramenta, com atendimento oferecido por clínicos gerais especialistas, incluindo cardiologistas, pediatras e ginecologistas .

Ao término do atendimento, o paciente recebe as prescrições médicas e os pedidos de exames no próprio dispositivo móvel

Segundo a gestão do sistema, dados do paciente são protegidos por sigilo e há protocolos de encaminhamento para unidades de emergência caso a equipe médica detecte quadros de maior gravidade durante as transmissões.

Para atender usuários sem acesso à internet de qualidade ou com pouca familiaridade com smartphones, a Unidade Básica de Saúde (UBS) Macapaba abriu um espaço de suporte presencial. Na sala, técnicos de enfermagem auxiliam no download, no cadastro e na realização das chamadas.

A diretora da UBS Macapaba, Maralibiane, afirmou que o objetivo da sala física é evitar a exclusão de moradores que enfrentam barreiras tecnológicas.

"A sala foi implantada para dar suporte principalmente a idosos e pessoas com dificuldade de acesso à tecnologia. O aplicativo vem para somar, mas não substitui as consultas presenciais na unidade", explicou a diretora

Dois motociclistas, de 21 e 52 anos, ficaram feridos em uma batida em um cruzamento na rua dos Carijós, no bairro Caramuru, em Patos de Minas , no Alto Paranaíba. O acidente aconteceu na tarde de quinta-feira (8), e os dois foram encaminhados para atendimento médico.

Câmeras de monitoramento registraram a colisão, que deixou os dois motociclistas caídos no chão. Assista o vídeo acima.

Segundo as informações do Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu), ao chegarem no local do acidente, os dois motociclistas apresentavam escoriações pelo corpo e foram imobilizados.

Os dois homens foram foram levados para a Santa Casa de Misericórdia (SCM) em Patos de Minas e o estado de saúde deles não foi informado.

articles.title: Paciente com anemia grave em Juiz de Fora recebe sangue raro do Ceará | G1
articles.standfirst: Doador está entre as seis pessoas cadastradas no Brasil com sangue compatível com o paciente, que passou por um transplante de rim. Viagem foi de mais de 2 mil quilômetros.
articles.summary: Doador está entre as 6 pessoas cadastradas no Brasil com sangue compatível com o paciente, que passou por um transplante de rim. Viagem foi de mais de 2 mil km.
articles.body:
Santa Casa de Juiz de Fora — Foto: Juliana Netto/g1

Um paciente de 63 anos internado na Santa Casa de Misericórdia de Juiz de Fora , com anemia grave após passar por um transplante de rim, recebeu uma doação de sangue raro enviada do Ceará.

A distância entre o estado nordestino e a cidade mineira é de mais de 2 mil quilômetros. Para que o sangue chegasse a tempo, foi necessário transportá-lo de avião até a Região Metropolitana de Belo Horizonte e, depois, de carro por cerca de 300 km até Juiz de Fora.

Além da longa distância, a busca pelo sangue foi um desafio: o doador está entre as apenas seis pessoas cadastradas no Brasil com sangue compatível com o paciente.

Segundo o hospital, que é referência em transplante de rim no país, necessidade da transfusão foi identificada pela equipe técnica da Agência Transfusional da Santa Casa durante os exames preparatórios.

Na avaliação, foi detectado um anticorpo no organismo do paciente que reagia contra as hemácias, as células vermelhas do sangue. Embora estivesse estável, o paciente precisava da transfusão porque apresentava níveis baixos de hemoglobina.

Exames complementares identificaram que o organismo dele produz anticorpos contra o antígeno Jsb, uma característica presente na superfície das hemácias da maioria das pessoas. Por isso, ele precisa receber sangue de um doador que não tenha esse marcador, o que torna a busca por compatibilidade mais difícil.

🔎 O antígeno Jsb é uma proteína presente na superfície das hemácias, as células vermelhas do sangue. Como a maioria das pessoas tem esse marcador, encontrar um doador compatível pode ser difícil. No caso do paciente de Juiz de Fora , o organismo produz anticorpos que reconhecem o Jsb como uma ameaça e podem atacar as hemácias que apresentam essa característica. Por isso, ele precisa receber sangue de alguém que não tenha o antígeno.

A doadora chegou cedo ao hemocentro do Ceará na quinta-feira (8) para realizar a coleta. Às 18h, a bolsa de sangue embarcou em um avião comercial, sob os cuidados do piloto.

O material chegou ao Aeroporto de Confins, na Região Metropolitana de Belo Horizonte, no início da manhã desta sexta (9). De lá, seguiu de carro por quase 300km até Juiz de Fora.

Conforme a assessoria da Santa Casa de Misericórdida, a transfusão aconteceu à tarde, conforme previsto.

Seis possíveis doadores em todo o Brasil

A busca pelo sangue compatível com o paciente de Juiz de Fora chegou ao cadastro nacional de doadores raros, que reúne 2.032 pessoas. O pedido foi feito ao Ministério da Saúde na quarta-feira (7), e a lista indicou apenas seis possíveis doadores em todo o Brasil.

O doador do Ceará foi avisado às 22h ainda da quarta e confirmou que poderia fazer a doação. O hemocentro do estado repetiu os testes para confirmar a compatibilidade e acelerou os exames para descartar doenças como HIV e hepatites B e C. A identidade do doador é mantida em sigilo.

articles.title: Trens da Linha 8-Diamante, da ViaMobilidade, são paralisados após falha no sistema de energia em Barueri | G1
articles.standfirst: Problema afetou as estações Carapicuíba e Sagrado Coração, na Grande SP, no início da noite desta sexta-feira (9). Concessionária informou que ônibus da operação Paese foram acionados para atender o trecho entre Santa Terezinha e Itapevi.
articles.summary: Problema afetou as estações Carapicuíba e Sagrado Coração, na Grande SP, no início da noite desta sexta-feira (9). Concessionária informou que ônibus da operação Paese foram acionados para atender o trecho entre Santa Terezinha e Itapevi.
articles.body:
Uma falha no sistema de energia da estação Barueri, da Linha 8-Diamante da ViaMobilidade, provocou a paralisação de trens entre as estações Carapicuíba e Sagrado Coração, na Grande São Paulo , no início da noite desta sexta-feira (9).

A concessionária informou que ônibus da operação Paese foram acionados para atender o trecho entre Santa Terezinha e Itapevi e que agentes de Atendimento e Segurança (AAS) orientam os clientes nas plataformas.

Segundo a empresa, equipes de manutenção foram as acionadas para "restabelecer a operação o mais breve possível".

Vídeos feitos por passageiros mostram que as estações afetadas estão com superlotação de pessoas ( veja acima ).

Por volta das 19h, a ViaMobilidade informou que a operação da Linha 8-Diamante foi integralmente restabelecida, "mas o fluxo nas plataformas segue em processo de regularização"

Mais cedo, a circulação dos trens da Linha 1-Azul do Metrô de São Paulo também foi afetada após uma interferência na via na estação Vergueiro para a retirada de um veículo de manutenção.

Segundo a empresa, a linha entrou em processo de normalização às 6h06, e houve reflexos na Linha 3-Vermelha.

Os trens circularam com velocidade reduzida e maior tempo de parada desde as 4h40. O problema estava concentrado entre as estações São Joaquim e Paraíso, as composições circularam por via singela. No restante da linha, a circulação ocorreu pelas duas vias.

Na operação em via singela, os trens utilizam uma única via para circular nos dois sentidos, de forma alternada. A medida pode aumentar o intervalo entre as composições e provocar atrasos.

Vagões lotados na Linha 3-Vermelha, em razão da falha na Linha 1-Azul do Metrô, na manhã desta sexta-feira (9). — Foto: Herminio Bernardo/TV Globo

O Sistema Paese chegou a ser acionado na Linha 1-Azul, com dez veículos para servir o trecho entre Sé e Ana Rosa, em razão de um trem de manutenção que ficou preso no túnel.

Por causa da ocorrência, os trens da Linha 3-Vermelha também circularam com restrição de velocidade.

Para reforçar o atendimento aos passageiros, o Metrô acionou o sistema de ônibus gratuito Paese no trecho entre as estações Ana Rosa e Sé.

O Metrô pediu desculpas aos passageiros pelos transtornos provocados.

A Linha 5-Lilás também enfrentou problemas na manhã desta sexta (9) devido a uma falha de equipamento de via na região de Santo Amaro. O Paese também foi acionado, com 60 ônibus.

Segundo a concessionária Motiva, os trens estavam com circulação via única na estação Santo Amaro e maiores intervalos entre as estações.

"As equipes de manutenção estão no local e trabalham para regularizar a operação o mais breve possível. A operação PAESE foi acionada. Agentes de atendimento e segurança estão no local para auxiliar os clientes no que for necessário", diz a Motiva.

articles.title: 'Inspired by 9/11’: Omani flydubai co-pilot planned to crash jet into Israeli airport, claims UAE
articles.summary: The Omani co-pilot of a Flydubai passenger aircraft planned to seize control of a Dubai-Tel Aviv flight and crash it into a terminal at Israel’s Ben
articles.body: The Omani co-pilot of a Flydubai passenger aircraft planned to seize control of a Dubai-Tel Aviv flight and crash it into a terminal at Israel’s Ben Gurion Airport in a suicide attack inspired by the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks, the United Arab Emirates’ attorney general said on Friday.According to the UAE state news agency WAM, Attorney General Hamad Saif Al Shamsi said the findings emerged from an investigation launched on October 1 into the September 30 incident involving Flydubai flight FZ1073.The co-pilot’s plan was thwarted by the aircraft's Indian captain, Smit Machchhar, who prevented him from taking control of the aircraft.UAE public prosecutors believe the alleged plot was inspired by the September 11 attacks on the United States, UAE state news agency WAM reported.Investigators said the suspect had taken two earlier flights to Tel Aviv to “familiarise himself with the flight route and the airport”.The 29-year-old suspect, identified in earlier reports as Hamam al-Hammami, allegedly intended to cause the greatest possible loss of life, according to findings released by the UAE attorney general.The September 30 incident ended with an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia. The co-pilot allegedly attacked the captain with an emergency crash axe and attempted to seize control of the aircraft. The incident caused the jet to plunge 16,000 feet in 30 seconds, according to the account provided in reports on the investigation.Al Shamsi said the suspect had previously worked for several airlines in different countries, including Oman Air and Royal Air Maroc, before joining Flydubai in January 2026.The Jerusalem Post reported that the investigation found the alleged plot was premeditated and that the suspect’s shift towards extremism began in 2017, while he was studying in Australia.Earlier, two Israeli officials familiar with the investigation had told news agency Reuters, that the co-pilot had told UAE interrogators he planned the attack before being hired by Flydubai.A third source briefed on the UAE investigation told Reuters that the suspect had also intended to hijack and crash an earlier flight to Tel Aviv but did not carry out the plan.“It was not immediately clear why the co-pilot changed his mind on that previous flight,” Reuters reported, citing the source, who added that the co-pilot was thought to have known someone onboard.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'City can't be brought to a halt': Delhi Police's rationale for restrictions ahead of CJP stir
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Delhi police has justified its restrictions on a proposed protest by the Cockroach Janta Party at Jantar Mantar, citing past violence, alleged
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi police has justified its restrictions on a proposed protest by the Cockroach Janta Party at Jantar Mantar, citing past violence, alleged assaults on women constables and the need to maintain public safety. The police said the organisers were proceeding without permission and stressed that the temporary curbs were necessary to prevent overcrowding and keep the capital functioning.In a statement posted on X, the force said, "The right to protest must be protected, but so must the right of a city to function safely. Responsible policing is about balancing both."The police cited violence during a protest in July to explain its concerns.According to the statement, permission had been granted for a one-day demonstration, but it continued for a month. More than 200 police personnel were injured, while over 2,000 people with criminal antecedents joined the protest, contributing to the violence.The police said the situation eventually spiralled out of control, leading to clashes in which students were also injured. It added that women constables had been molested and assaulted by protesters at Jantar Mantar in the past week.Crowd management and public safetyThe police also pointed to the limited capacity of Jantar Mantar, saying the site could accommodate only 1,000 people at a time. It said restrictions were needed to prevent overcrowding and protect protesters, residents, shopkeepers and others in the area.The force said Delhi Police had to balance the right to protest with the safety of residents and the capital's economic interests. It added that the city could not be brought to a halt every time a demonstration took place.According to the statement, seeking permission allows authorities to estimate crowd numbers and plan traffic diversions, emergency access and safe movement around the protest site. The police said this would help demonstrators raise their concerns while allowing residents, workers and businesses to continue with their daily activities.Police cite legal position on unauthorised protestsThe police said the Cockroach Janta Party was proceeding with its planned gathering without permission. Citing the Supreme Court's position, the statement said a protest held without permission was unlawful and participants could face prosecution.It added that organisers were responsible for explaining the legal position to those they invited to attend."The restrictions being put in place today are temporary. They are intended to regulate the flow of people, prevent overcrowding and keep protesters, residents, shopkeepers and others in the area safe," the statement read.The police said the precautions were intended to ensure that people could raise their concerns peacefully without compromising public safety or disrupting the functioning of the city.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.body: TOI Correspondent from Washington: “His in-laws were indentured servants and his wife is an anchor baby.” That was one of the barbs ricocheting around social media after US vice president JD Vance accused microsoft of replacing american workers with "foreign indentured servants" - shortly before his boss honored the company’s India-born CEO, Satya Nadella, at the white house.Vance may have intended to put Silicon Valley in the dock with what was perceived as a slut that invited a withering response from New Delhi. Instead, he opened several lines of fire at once with his use of a colonial-era term - from Indian professionals, who regard H-1B visas as a route to opportunity rather than servitude; from tech giants, who credit immigrants with building some of America’s most valuable businesses; and from social-media users delighted to discover an immigration controversy in the vice-president’s own family, one highlighted by a rabid section of the MAGA base.The reference to Vance’s in-laws was pointed, if imprecise. His wife, Usha Vance, was born in California in 1986 to Krish and Lakshmi Chilukuri, immigrants from Andhra Pradesh. The family settled in the San Diego area, where her father pursued an engineering career and her mother became a molecular biologist. Usha Chilukuri went on to Yale, a school founded with donation from a notorious Bostonian, Elihu Yale, who pillaged India as the governor general of Madras; she met JD Vance at Yale law school.In other words, the family’s publicly documented story is one of immigration, higher education and professional achievement. There is no established evidence that her parents were “indentured labourers” since their coming to America predated the H1-B program that began in 1990, but their route to US residency was not very different - from academia to employment. Calling Usha an “anchor baby” is equally misleading; she was born in California and is a US citizen by birth under the constitutional rule generally applicable to people born on American soil.Meanwhile, Microsoft’s response directly challenges the impression that its H-1B figures represent thousands of new foreign hires. Of approximately 6,000 H-1B applications it filed in the last fiscal year, the company said, 80% were extensions or changes of status for existing employees. These were not applications to bring in new workers. The remaining filings concerned people already legally present in the US, who chose to work for Microsoft; the company said these employees amounted to about 1% of its US workforce.Microsoft also said it pays H-1B employees the same as other employees doing comparable work, and that its wages rank among the highest in the technology sector. While the figures do not establish that microsoft never displaces American workers, or that every H-1B employer complies with the law, they do challenge the simple Vance arithmetic in which 6,000 layoffs plus 6,000 visa applications automatically equal 6,000 replacements of American workers deserving "American jobs."There is another inconvenient detail for Vance’s argument; Nadella himself immigrated from India and built his career in the US, going on to become microsoft’s CEO - only the third after Bill Gates and Steve Ballmer - in 2014 after joining the company in 1992. While career is hardly proof that every visa holder is indispensable, it is a reminder that the immigrant talent pool Vance is attacking has also helped produce the very American corporate success he wants to defend. Microsoft has grown more than 12x (market cap growing from $ 300 billion to almost $ 4 trillion) in the time Nadella has helmed the company and many American retirement accounts have grown on the ballast provided by such tech giants.Among the most pointed responses to Vance’s slight came from Shobhit Mathur, Co-founder and Vice chancellor of Rishihood university and IIT alum. Recalling his early days at Amazon in an H-1B role, Mathur wrote on X that he was part of the initial team that built Amazon Web Services (AWS), which he described as now contributing more than 60% of Amazon’s profits. His post’s central argument was simple: around a hundred H-1B holders were part of that early team, and the company’s subsequent transformation would have looked very different without them. “Good luck building companies and wealth without these ‘indentured servants’,” he scoffed.The timing of Vance’s broadside has prompted another question: why is the administration escalating its campaign now, rather than earlier in Trump’s term, or for that matter, during his first term? The answer may be a mixture of policy and politics. The administration has already taken steps to tighten the H-1B program, which even some of its supporters say had been gamed by some operators, and the latest action gives Vance an opportunity to demonstrate that the crackdown is reaching powerful corporations, not just migrants at the bottom of the labour market. Naming Microsoft and suspending its access to a green-card process creates a visible target, although Vance and co have conspicuously let amazon, which processes more H1Bs than Microsoft, off the hook.The final twist of irony came in the wee hours of Friday even as Vance’s gibe about “indentured servants” echoed across the world, where several nations are led by descendants of immigrant laborers. The Nobel committee awarded the 2026 peace prize to Navi Pillay, the South African jurist of Indian Tamil descent, snubbing a non-indentured leader, who has literally been begging for it.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2025, Maine’s Joan Alexander received her college degree at 88, more than six decades after enrolling and 44 years after completing comparable work
articles.summary: Joan Alexander, at the age of 88, celebrates her graduation from the University of Maine, receiving her Bachelor of Science in Education 66 years after starting the program. This inspiring story highlights her journey to fulfill her educational dreams after decades of family commitments.
articles.body: Joan Alexander received the Bachelor of Science in Education from the University of Maine in 2025, more than six decades after she first began the program. At 88, she remains likely the oldest recipient of the undergraduate degree in the institution’s 160-year history.Alexander, intending to become a teacher, had entered the University of Maine in the late 1950s and was expected to graduate in 1959. She finished all other degree requirements, but the university's policy against student-teaching while pregnant forced her to leave just before graduation. She had her first child, Bonnie. An alternative route emerged through her youngest daughter, Tracy, who contacted the College of Education and Human Development to ask whether her mother's unfinished degree could be resolved.University found her later preschool work met the missing requirement Justin Dimmel, associate dean for academics and student engagement in the College of Education and Human Development, examined Alexander's academic history with colleagues to determine whether the outstanding requirement could be satisfied by her later experience. The review found that Alexander, in 1980-81, had undertaken work which was comparable to student teaching roughly two decades after her original studies. She had worked full-time at a home-based preschool program in Southwest Harbor, Maine, where she taught preschool-aged children on gross and fine motor skills, verbal communication, imaginative play and early literacy.After the work was reviewed, the college determined that a year of full-time employment with preschool children was akin to the student-teaching requirement she had been unable to complete in the 1950s. That finding made it possible to award Alexander the degree without requiring her to repeat the academic work she had already completed. Dimmel said the process involved administrators from across the university, and Alexander's commitment to complete her undergraduate education served as an inspiration to those involved.Alexander was finally recognized during the University of Maine’s undergraduate commencement ceremony on May 11, 2025. While she couldn't attend the ceremony in person, her daughter Tracy and granddaughter Isabel Beck attended on her behalf. The story had garnered attention from media outlets across the United States and India while the president highlighted Alexander’s story in her commencement remarks.A degree that completed a family milestone The recognition carried significance beyond the academic merit, as Alexander’s parents had not completed college, making higher education particularly important to her. Meanwhile, her husband and four daughters had all earned college degrees, leaving her as the only member of her immediate family without one.For much of the intervening decades, Alexander’s time was devoted to her family, consisting of her husband, Jim, and their four daughters. Jim served in the U.S. Coast Guard which frequently kept him at sea for months at a time, which made Alexander the sole caretaker. Following Jim's retirement, the couple settled in Southwest Harbor where Alexander devoted time to her church and the local library and occasionally helped at the elementary school. Eventually, she and Jim moved to New Hampshire, where they now live with one of their daughters.Alexander had long wanted the work she completed as a student to be recognized rather than left unfinished. “I didn’t realize that it would mean so much to me, but I now feel that a hole in my heart has been healed,” she said to the University of Maine. For her daughter the commencement was significant because she attended the event with her own daughter and saw her mother’s long-unfinished education being formally recognized. After receiving the degree, Alexander offered advice to others pursuing higher education, encouraging them to find something of interest and to pursue it.You use AI every day. articles.summary: A man in Florida has been arrested after authorities alleged that he was running a business selling hallucinogenic cacti and mushrooms through Facebook
articles.body: A man in Florida has been arrested after authorities alleged that he was running a business selling hallucinogenic cacti and mushrooms through Facebook Marketplace. Investigators seized 131 live plants, approximately 50 pounds of mescaline-containing cacti and 1.5 pounds of psilocybin mushrooms during a search of his home in Riverview, according to the Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office.Zachary Diaz, 32, was arrested following a search warrant executed by the sheriff's office's Opioid Overdose Investigation Section on October 1, 2026. The search took place at a property in the 5500 block of Coolidge Street in Riverview, Florida.According to investigators, Diaz was allegedly operating a business selling mescaline-containing cacti, commonly known as peyote, along with psilocybin mushrooms. Authorities said the products were advertised for sale on Facebook Marketplace.131 live plants and hallucinogenic substances seizedThe search led to the recovery of 131 live plants, as well as equipment and supplies allegedly used for cultivation and manufacturing. Investigators also seized approximately 50 pounds of mescaline-containing cacti and 1.5 pounds of psilocybin mushrooms, the sheriff's office said.Announcing the arrest on social media, the Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office issued a warning against using Facebook Marketplace to sell hallucinogenic substances.“Selling hallucinogens on Facebook Marketplace? Not in Hillsborough County,” the department wrote in its post, outlining the findings of the investigation and the charges against Diaz.Authorities said Diaz already had outstanding warrants connected to the investigation when the search was conducted.What charges does Zachary Diaz face?According to the sheriff's office, Diaz faces three counts of possession of a controlled substance with intent to sell, manufacture or deliver within 1,000 feet of a church. He also faces three counts of delivery of a controlled substance within 1,000 feet of a church.In addition, Diaz has been charged with two counts of manufacturing a controlled substance.The charges relate to the alleged sale, delivery and manufacture of controlled substances. The sheriff's office has not reported a conviction, and the allegations remain subject to the legal process.The investigation was conducted by the Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office's Opioid Overdose Investigation Section. articles.title: Avianca flight makes emergency landing in Miami after severe turbulence, at least 8 injured
articles.summary: An Avianca flight had to make an emergency landing in Miami early Friday due to extreme turbulence, injuring at least eight people.
articles.body: An Avianca flight had to make an emergency landing in Miami early Friday due to extreme turbulence, injuring at least eight people.Miami-Dade fire rescue said that seven people were transported to nearby hospitals in ambulances, and one person was sent to a trauma center with serious injuries, after the jet touched down just after 3 AM in the morning on Friday.According to the airline, nine people—six passengers and three staff members—were impacted by the turbulence and required medical attention.According to the Federal Aviation Administration, the Airbus A320 had to divert to Miami, when the Avianca aircraft was traveling from Medellin, Colombia, to John F. Kennedy International Airport in New York.According to Avianca, the passengers, who were not hurt transported to New York early on Friday. "The safety of our customers, and employees is, and will remain, the foundation of our operations," the airline stated.Although severe injuries from in-flight turbulence are uncommon, experts believe that if climate change modifies the jet stream, they may become more frequent. According to the International Air Transport Association, there were almost 25% more complaints of turbulence occurrences last year.24 people were hospitalised last summer, after a Delta air lines flight encountered severe turbulence caused by a thunderstorm over Wyoming.According to the National Transportation Safety Board, passengers, and flight attendants were thrown against the aircraft’s ceiling with such force that some interior panels cracked.They then fell back to the floor before being tossed upwards again. The seat belt sign was switched off at the time, and some passengers were standing while cabin crew served drinks when the aircraft hit the turbulence, according to the News Agency AP.At least 20 passengers have filed lawsuits against Delta over the incident, alleging that the airline could have avoided the severe weather.The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) recommends that passengers keep their seat belts fastened, whenever possible to protect themselves from unexpected turbulence.You use AI every day. articles.title: Rahul Gandhi's claim that President Murmu accepted 'vote theft' allegation incorrect: Report
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's claim suggesting President Droupadi Murmu accepted assertions of 'vote theft' is incorrect, sources told news
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's claim suggesting President Droupadi Murmu accepted assertions of 'vote theft' is incorrect, sources told news agency PTI."Unfortunate that President of India is being dragged into controversy raised by opposition," sources further told PTI.Earlier, terming Gandhi's claim "unfortunate and bizarre", BJP spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi said: "He is lying.""His claim that the president has accepted his allegations demonstrates the malicious cycle Rahul Gandhi has been orchestrating, turning every constitutional body into a victim of his politics. It now appears that he has crossed all limits," he told reporters.Trivedi said that only "someone", other than the INDIA bloc delegation, could reveal what actually transpired in the meeting."The way Rahul Gandhi spoke, the body language and facial expressions of the leaders standing beside him clearly suggested that what was being said likely bore no relation to the truth. Rahul Gandhi's past track record also reflects this pattern," the BJP Rajya Sabha MP said.Gandhi's claim not only "seems strange" but also reeks more of politics than truth, he added.After meeting the President, Rahul Gandhi had said, "The main thing is that I expected the President of India to deny that 'vote chori' was taking place. I expected her to say that India has a free and fair electoral system. I was shocked and stunned that the President of India accepted what we said".Regarding the President's response during their interaction, Rahul Gandhi said, "I sat in quite an unbelievable meeting. First, we took a memorandum to the President of India. In that memorandum, we clearly stated that the Prime Minister, HM Amit Shah, and CEC Gyanesh Kumar had conspired to destroy Indian democracy. The President in no way denied what we said, questioned what we said, or argued what we said."He futher said: "She accepted our statement and then told us that we needed to provide her with proof of 'election chori'. I said that the evidence of 'election chori' is known to the entire country. State after state has been stolen. The 2024 election was stolen, and yet the President wants us to submit proof to her. This same group of people will be very happy to present the evidence of 'election chori' that we have collected to the President of India when she is ready to accept it..."Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Naresh Bhatt trial in Virginia: Friend alleges abuse, financial control in Nepali woman Mamta Kafle Bhatt’s disappearance case, mother breaks down in court
articles.summary: A close friend of Mamta Kafle Bhatt testified that her husband, Naresh Bhatt, allegedly hit and controlled her in the months before she disappeared from
articles.body: A close friend of Mamta Kafle Bhatt testified that her husband, Naresh Bhatt, allegedly hit and controlled her in the months before she disappeared from their Virginia home in July 2024. Mamta’s mother also took the stand, recounting how her daily conversations with her daughter suddenly stopped.A close friend of Mamta Kafle Bhatt told a Virginia court that Naresh Bhatt had physically abused and controlled his wife in the months before she disappeared, as prosecutors presented witness testimony in his murder trial.Sarita Neupane, a friend of Mamta, testified that she had seen her distressed several months before her disappearance and brought her into her home. Mamta subsequently stayed with Neupane for nearly two weeks while experiencing marital difficulties with Naresh, according to testimony reported by local media.Neupane told the court that Naresh had allegedly hit Mamta during an argument over household cleaning, leaving a large bruise on her face. The injury was so visible that Mamta had to reschedule a traditional ceremony marking the couple’s daughter’s first consumption of solid food, the friend testified.The testimony offered jurors a glimpse into the couple’s relationship before Mamta, a nurse and mother of a young child, vanished from their home in Manassas Park, Virginia, in July 2024.Neupane also alleged that Naresh exercised financial and personal control over his wife. According to her testimony, he restricted Mamta’s access to money, shut off her cellphone and would not allow her to drive his car or obtain a vehicle of her own.The friend said she was trying to help Mamta become more independent by assisting her in setting up a bank account and beginning the process of obtaining US citizenship. Mamta was a green card holder.Mamta’s mother recounts last conversations with daughterMamta’s mother, Gita Kafle, also testified, describing how she lost contact with her daughter in July 2024.Kafle told the court that she and Mamta spoke every day, usually in the morning and evening. Those conversations suddenly stopped, prompting her to try reaching her daughter repeatedly.According to her testimony, Kafle also attempted to contact Naresh after she was unable to reach Mamta for several days. When he eventually spoke with her, he said Mamta had gone to stay with friends, Kafle told the court.The account was an emotional part of the proceedings, with Mamta’s mother becoming visibly upset as she recalled the sudden break in their daily contact.Kafle later travelled from Nepal to Northern Virginia to help search for her daughter and seek answers about what had happened.Mamta disappeared in July 2024Mamta, a registered nurse who worked at UVA Health Prince William Medical Center, was last known to have been in contact with people close to her in late July 2024. She failed to report for her shift on August 1, raising concerns among colleagues.Her supervisor subsequently requested a police welfare check at the couple’s home in Manassas Park on August 2.The disappearance triggered a search involving police, relatives, friends and members of the local Nepali community. Investigators eventually arrested Naresh, who has been accused of killing his wife and concealing and defiling her body.Mamta’s remains have never been recovered.Prosecutors cite blood and DNA evidenceDuring opening statements in the trial, prosecutors alleged that Naresh killed Mamta and dismembered her body before attempting to dispose of evidence.Deputy Commonwealth’s Attorney Matthew Sweet told jurors that Naresh had given a saw to a landscaper working in the neighbourhood after Mamta disappeared. According to the prosecution, the landscaper later brought the saw to police, and forensic testing found Mamta’s blood and DNA on it.Prosecutors have also pointed to blood evidence recovered from the couple’s home, electronic records, internet searches and surveillance footage as part of their case.They have alleged that video shows Naresh disposing of large, heavy-duty garbage bags in dumpsters and trash compactors in Northern Virginia. Prosecutors believe the bags may have contained Mamta’s remains.The prosecution is seeking to establish what happened despite the absence of a body, relying on forensic findings, digital evidence and witness accounts to build its case.Defence challenges prosecution’s accountNaresh has pleaded not guilty to charges including first-degree murder, concealing a dead body and defiling a dead body. He is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty in court.His defence attorney, Tracey Lenox, has argued that the prosecution must establish its case through evidence rather than speculation. In opening statements, the defence highlighted what it described as gaps in the evidence and questioned whether prosecutors could prove their allegations beyond a reasonable doubt.The trial is being heard in Prince William County Circuit Court, with testimony expected to continue over the coming weeks.The case has drawn widespread attention, particularly among members of the Nepali community in the United States, as Mamta’s family continues to seek answers about her disappearance.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2018, Ron Burkle bought Bob Hope's 5-acre Los Angeles estate for $15 million; after restoring it while preserving Hope's oak library and golf hole, he sold it for $26 million in 2023
articles.summary: An iconic piece of Hollywood history in Los Angeles has changed hands for $26 million (£20 million) after undergoing a sensitive multi-year restoration
articles.body: An iconic piece of Hollywood history in Los Angeles has changed hands for $26 million (£20 million) after undergoing a sensitive multi-year restoration project. American businessman Ron Burkle acquired the sprawling five-acre Toluca Lake compound that once belonged to the legendary entertainer Bob Hope in 2018 for $15 million (£11.5 million). Following a meticulous restoration aimed at preserving its architectural heritage, Burkle listed the property and successfully closed the sale in early 2023, as confirmed by property records and listing agency details. The transaction marks a significant profit on the historic residence, which Burkle saved from potential subdivision and demolition by property developers when he purchased it from the Bob and Dolores Hope Foundation.Historic grounds preserved from divisionThe historic estate, located at 10346 Moorpark Street, served as the primary residence for Bob Hope and his wife, Dolores, for over six decades. Originally constructed in 1939 by architect Robert Finkelhor and subsequently redesigned in the 1950s by Hollywood Regency master John Elgin Woolf, the French Revival compound was long considered the centerpiece of Toluca Lake. When the property first entered the real estate market following Dolores Hope's death, local preservationists and community members voiced concern over its fate. The extensive plot offered ample space for residential developers looking to divide the five acres into multiple sub-plots for modern housing. According to reporting by Realtor.com, Burkle secured the property in 2018 at a discounted price point after committing to maintain the integrity of the original structure rather than razing the grounds. Proceeds from that initial $15 million sale were directed entirely to the Bob and Dolores Hope Foundation to support charitable works for military veterans and families in need.Restoring classic Hollywood architectureRather than modernising the estate beyond recognition, Burkle launched an extensive restoration project designed to update the infrastructure while maintaining key historic components. According to real estate platform Pricey Pads and property details from listing brokerage The Agency, the 15,000-square-foot main house features ten bedrooms and extensive living spaces tailored to high-society entertaining. Interior restoration work preserved original architectural features, including the oak-panelled library where the famed entertainer kept scripts and memorabilia from his 50-year career with the United Service Organizations (USO) and his fourteen stints hosting the Academy Awards. The grounds themselves retained several custom outdoor elements commissioned by Hope during his lifetime. These include a private one-hole golf course complete with a sand bunker, designed specifically so the golf enthusiast could practice his game at home. The five-acre parcel also retains a two-story guest house, staff quarters, a formal rose garden, and an outdoor swimming pool alongside an indoor pool complex.High-value resale in Toluca LakeBurkle initially placed the fully restored estate back on the market in 2022 with an asking price of $29 million (£22.3 million). Listing agents Kevin Dees and Sebastian Spader of The Agency handled the high-profile offering, positioning the compound as a turnkey historic landmark. Real estate transaction data shows the property officially settled in March 2023 for $26 million, solidifying one of the highest residential sales recorded in the San Fernando Valley sub-market. The successful sale underscores sustained buyer appetite for restored mid-century celebrity compounds across Southern California, where large acreage remains exceptionally rare. The Los Angeles Conservancy continues to recognise the residence as a landmark property of architectural and cultural significance for the city's entertainment heritage.You use AI every day. articles.body: Reginald “Reggie,” also known as “Lil Rodney Son,” has responded to Kai Cenat’s threat to sue him over allegations involving streamer RaKai. In a YouTube video posted on October 8, 2026, Reggie repeated his claims against Cenat and said he was saving his evidence for court. He also accused Cenat of having too much influence over Twitch and claimed that he could no longer stream on the platform. Cenat had threatened legal action after Reggie made the allegations on September 30. Neither the allegations nor Reggie’s claims about Twitch have been independently confirmed.Reggie Doubles Down on Allegations Against Kai CenatThe dispute began on September 30, when Reggie accused Cenat of grooming RaKai and encouraging him to behave inappropriately for attention. These are serious allegations, and Reggie has not publicly established them as facts.Cenat responded during a Twitch livestream the same day. He challenged Reggie to take his evidence to the police and said he planned to sue him.“This is so serious. This is what I want you to do, Reggie. Tomorrow, when you wake up, call the cops. Call the cops and show them the evidence. Because guess what? I’m calling the cops. Yeah. Yeah, I’m suing you, brother. I’m suing you, bro.”Reggie addressed that threat in his five-minute, 11-second YouTube video titled THE TRUTH ABOUT EVERYTHING PART 3. Instead of backing away from his claims, he said he was ready to face Cenat in court.“Kai Cenat is a PDF, and everybody knows it! I don't understand how y'all can't see it! He's grooming RaKai, and it is in front of our face, bro!”Reggie then questioned why viewers kept asking him to show proof. He referred to the allegations surrounding Sean “Diddy” Combs before explaining why he was holding back his own material.“Listen to me when I tell y'all this - if Kai says he is going to sue me, I'm saving my evidence for court. Let's do it then! I know everything! And I'm not going to lie to ruin no man's reputation. I know everything!”Although Reggie said he had evidence, he did not present proof establishing his allegations in the video. His statements remain accusations, not verified findings. articles.body: NEW DELHI: In the ongoing war of words over the ongoing satellite communication services in India by Starlink, Elon Musk has launched his shrillest ever attack on Mukesh Ambani.In a late night post on X, the Starlink boss said: "Dear Prime Minister Ambani, please accept my humble apologies for not realising that you are the real boss of India. Naturally, you would prefer to maintain your monopolistic exploitation of the great people of India, but would you nonetheless consider allowing Starlink to compete?""There are many areas of India, as there are in all countries, with no Internet access, which denies children the opportunity for education and for small businesses the opportunity to sell their goods to a global market. Starlink would change their lives for the better. Also, Starlink has proven to be essential for saving lives during natural disasters throughout the world, when all other communications systems have failed, so you would also be helping save men, women and children throughout India," Musk's latest post said.The fresh expression of anger over the alleged delay in approving satellite communication services in India - something all the three licence holders, with the other two being Sunil Bharti-backed Eutelsat OneWeb and Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Jio are facing - began Wednesday and he has been cranking the heat each passing day since then.On day one, he accused "certain oligarchs" of "blocking" Starlink's entry to India without naming anyone but saying "you can guess who they are." The second day, he followed up by naming Ambani and asking, "is Ambani the real boss of India." And on day three, he said, "Dear Prime Minister Ambani."Govt has denied the charges. Telecom minister Jyotiraditya Scindia said at the India Mobile Congress: "There is a lot of conversation about a particular party (Starlink). But there are three parties (Mittal, Jio and Musk) that have got licenses... We are very clear on our stand. As and when govt decides the charge system on revenue basis that spectrum will be assigned to them and as and when they individually fulfil security conditions, they can start operations." Billionaire Jeff Bezos-led Amazon's Project Kuiper is eyeing a licence to do so."India does not allow monopoly in any sector, " the minister said."Govt is technology agnostic. Our job is to provide a bouquet of services. In a free market, it is upto the customers to choose which service they want to opt for and then which service provider with that service bouquet. Govt's responsibility is to lay out a predictable regulatory architecture so that companies can make their capex decisions," Scindia said.The minister further said that the Union govt is "close to taking the final decision with respect to (spectrum for satcom) pricing regime. TRAI has made some recommendations and the DoT is engaging with it on that".Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Florida ransomware expert said his company could decrypt attacks without paying hackers; prosecutors allege he charged victims more than $19 million while secretly sending over $8 million in ransom payments
articles.summary: A Florida cybersecurity expert who claimed his company could recover data locked by ransomware without paying hackers has been charged with fraud in the
articles.body: A Florida cybersecurity expert who claimed his company could recover data locked by ransomware without paying hackers has been charged with fraud in the United States. Federal prosecutors allege that Zohar Pinhasi, 50, secretly paid cybercriminals to obtain decryption keys while charging his clients much higher fees. According to the US Department of Justice, his company collected more than $19 million from clients and paid over $8 million in ransom payments.Pinhasi, who also used the names “Zack Silver” and “Zack Green,” owns MonsterCloud LLC, a Florida-based ransomware remediation company. He was arraigned on wire fraud charges in a federal court in Brooklyn on Wednesday after a grand jury in the Eastern District of New York indicted him on September 23.The allegations concern businesses that had already suffered ransomware attacks and approached MonsterCloud for help. Ransomware is a type of cyberattack in which criminals encrypt files, making them inaccessible, and demand payment to provide a decryption key. MonsterCloud presented itself as a company that could recover such files without giving money to the attackers.However, prosecutors allege that Pinhasi did not have the special technology he advertised. Instead, he contacted the same cybercriminals who had attacked his clients, paid them for decryption keys and charged the businesses substantially more than the ransom amounts.MonsterCloud claimed to recover encrypted dataAccording to the indictment, MonsterCloud promoted its services as an alternative to paying ransomware attackers. Its website warned businesses against paying ransom and claimed that its team could help recover encrypted information through specialised technology.The company said it used “proprietary tools” and “advanced decryption techniques” to restore access to affected files. These claims were particularly relevant to businesses whose data had become inaccessible following cyberattacks.MonsterCloud's website also stated that “our team specializes in helping businesses recover their data without succumbing to ransom demands.”Federal investigators, however, allege that the company did not possess the technology it claimed to use. Instead of independently decrypting the files, Pinhasi allegedly negotiated with the attackers and paid them to obtain decryption keys.MonsterCloud employees then used those keys in an attempt to restore the clients' encrypted files. Prosecutors say the clients were not told that their payments were being used to pay the criminals responsible for the original attacks. $150,000 for an $8,200 ransomOne transaction highlighted by prosecutors took place in August 2023. According to the Justice Department, Pinhasi paid approximately $8,200 to a cybercriminal to obtain a decryption key.However, he allegedly charged the affected client approximately $150,000 for the service, significantly more than the ransom payment.Investigators say this was part of a broader scheme in which MonsterCloud collected large fees while secretly paying ransomware attackers.Over the course of the alleged scheme, prosecutors say Pinhasi charged clients more than $19 million and sent over $8 million to cybercriminals.The indictment also raises questions about the company's advertising. MonsterCloud's website featured testimonials, including some from paid spokespersons.According to prosecutors, one such spokesperson contacted Pinhasi in May 2019 to ask whether MonsterCloud actually possessed proprietary software capable of decrypting ransomware-affected data.Pinhasi allegedly responded, “Monstercloud doesn’t hold any Proprietary technology [to] decrypt the ransomware data.”What US prosecutors said US Attorney Joseph Nocella Jr. for the Eastern District of New York accused Pinhasi of taking advantage of businesses that were already victims of cybercrime.“As alleged in the indictment, by falsely claiming to decrypt ransomware without paying off the ransomers, the defendant re-victimized his clients while extracting a hefty profit for himself,” Nocella said.FBI Assistant Director in Charge James C. Barnacle Jr. also alleged that Pinhasi failed to address the underlying cybersecurity threat while profiting from clients seeking assistance.“As alleged, Zohar Pinhasi claimed to fix ransomware while never remediating the underlying threat. Instead, he turned the victim's crisis into his own profit center,” Barnacle said.What charges does Pinhasi face?Pinhasi, a US and Israeli national from Hollywood, Florida, faces two counts of wire fraud and one count of wire fraud conspiracy.If convicted, he faces a maximum prison sentence of 20 years on each count. The case is being prosecuted by the US Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of New York and the Justice Department's Computer Crime and Intellectual Property Section.The Justice Department also referred to joint guidance from the FBI and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), which advises ransomware victims against paying attackers.The agencies warn that paying a ransom does not guarantee that encrypted data will be recovered, compromised systems will become secure or stolen information will not be leaked.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 1967, Georgia man Donnie Peek bought 150 acres and grew his property to 1,600 acres; decades later, a $3.2 billion pipeline route shifted to run 2.5 miles only through his land alone
articles.summary: A 79-year-old landowner in western Georgia is challenging a major energy company after learning that a $3.5 billion natural gas pipeline project was moved
articles.body: A 79-year-old landowner in western Georgia is challenging a major energy company after learning that a $3.5 billion natural gas pipeline project was moved away from a utility executive's home and routed across 2.5 miles of his private land. Donnie Peek bought his first 150-acre property in Muscogee County in 1967. Over the following decades, he expanded it into a 1,600-acre estate along the Chattahoochee River. After discovering the sudden route change, he filed a formal challenge with federal energy regulators. The Southern System Expansion 4 project is managed by Southern Natural Gas (SNG), a joint venture between energy companies Kinder Morgan and Southern Co. The project originally followed an existing utility easement that crossed four separate residential properties. Revised plans released earlier this year showed that developers had changed the route. The new plan sends the pipeline around the home of Chris Lane, a 25-year Southern Co. power plant manager, while placing the added burden on Peek's property.Sudden shift in the pipeline pathPeek was already used to having energy infrastructure on his land. A propane pipeline built in the 1960s already crossed his property. When developers first announced plans to put the new gas pipeline along that same easement, Peek did not object. Using existing rights of way is common in the industry because it can lower costs, limit damage to land, and reduce legal disputes. The revised plan, however, left the existing right of way as it came near Lane's home. The new route turns directly east along the edge of Lane's property. It then makes a sharp turn north to completely avoid his home. To cover the extra distance, developers added about 1,400 feet of pipe and placed 2.5 miles of continuous pipeline across Peek's land. According to The Atlanta Journal-Constitution, the detour adds millions of dollars to the cost of the interstate gas network. The system stretches 7,600 miles from Texas to the American South-East. In a March letter to Kinder Morgan's Land and Right-of-Way Department, Peek asked the company to return to the original straight route. The company rejected his request. In a formal response, it said that going back to the old route would "impact landowners and potentially more landowners."Rerouting raises questions over executive tiesPeek became concerned after learning that the neighbor whose property was spared from the pipeline worked as a senior manager overseeing power plants for a Southern Co. subsidiary. "That's when I said, 'Well, this thing smells,'" Peek told The Atlanta Journal-Constitution. "I think anybody with a little bit of sense puts it together … why they deviate this thing around, especially around this one property owner who is a pretty high up executive at the Southern Co." In an affidavit filed with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) on 28 August, Peek described a conversation with Lane. Peek said the executive told him that "there was 'no price at which he (Mr. Lane) would allow the pipeline to cross his property.'" Peek also said in his filing that a representative of Pinnacle Resources Group, which was working as an intermediary for SNG, told him that Lane's property could not be taken through eminent domain because of his position. SNG denied that Lane received special treatment. In a statement provided to The Atlanta Journal-Constitution, the company said: "There is no policy that exempts Southern Co. employees from this process." SNG said the route was changed to reduce the number of affected landowners from four to one. The company said the current route "represents the option that best balances overall landowner impacts with the project's operational needs."Buyout offers rejected by landownerAs talks continued, SNG offered Peek $300,000 (£225,000) for additional easement rights across his land if he could convince his neighbors to accept the original route. Peek could not reach an agreement with the other property owners. The company then offered to pay him the full cash amount directly if he agreed to the diverted 2.5-mile route. Peek rejected the offer. "That was the point when I told them, 'It's not about the money, it's just the fact that one person was involved getting it moved on my property instead of getting it to pass by his house,'" Peek told The Atlanta Journal-Constitution. Lane declined to comment publicly. However, emails obtained by The Atlanta Journal-Constitution show that he had earlier sent two alternative route proposals directly to Kinder Morgan. One proposal would have avoided the entire neighborhood by using an existing transmission line right of way near an Alabama power plant. Peek said he was completely left out of those discussions while the alternative routes were considered.Legal challenge moves to federal regulatorsAs construction preparations continue across the South-East, Peek's legal team has filed a petition with FERC asking the agency to rehear the case. FERC has regulatory authority over interstate natural gas pipelines. FERC has already given primary approval for the larger 7,600-mile system expansion. However, Peek's filing asks the agency to require SNG to return to the original straight-line easement. In his affidavit to federal regulators, Peek argued that returning to the original route "would have effectively eliminated the destruction of thousands of trees, shortened the pipe and more fairly shared the burden of the pipeline easement among the surrounding landowners." Allen Fore, an executive at Kinder Morgan, told The Atlanta Journal-Constitution that many engineering and environmental factors can lead to changes in pipeline routes. He added that company officials hope to speak directly with Peek after the legal reviews are completed. The petition is still being reviewed by FERC officials in Washington.You use AI every day. articles.title: London's 1952 smog killed thousands; four years later Britain passed a law that began ending its famous coal-filled 'pea soupers'
articles.summary: On a December morning in 1952, London disappeared beneath a blanket of dirty yellow fog.
articles.body: On a December morning in 1952, London disappeared beneath a blanket of dirty yellow fog. Visibility fell to only a few metres in places, public transport struggled and familiar streets became difficult to navigate. The air was not simply damp and murky. It was loaded with smoke, gases and particles from thousands of chimneys, trapped close to the ground by an unusual weather pattern. As reported by the Met Office, the smog lingered from 5 to 9 December, turning a familiar winter nuisance into a public health disaster. About 4,000 deaths were initially linked to the episode, although later estimates put the toll considerably higher. Four years later, Parliament passed the Clean Air Act 1956, introducing measures that began to change how smoke and coal burning were controlled in Britain's towns and cities.London's famous 'pea soup' fogs had been deadly long before 1952Fog was nothing new to Londoners by the middle of the 20th century. Industrialisation had made the capital's traditional mists far dirtier, as coal burning and factory emissions filled the atmosphere with particles and gases. The problem had been building for generations. A particularly thick smog was reported in London in December 1813, while a fog in December 1873 was followed by a 40% rise in London's death rate. Similar increases were recorded after several other major fogs during the late 19th and early 20th centuries.The East End was often particularly badly affected. It contained a dense mixture of homes and factories and was relatively low-lying, conditions that made it harder for polluted air to disperse. According to the research published in The Life of Breath in Literature, Culture and Medicine, titled ‘London Fog as Food: From Pabulum to Poison’, by 1952, London's thick, polluted fogs were already widely associated with the term “pea-souper”. But the conditions that developed that December were on a different scale.How cold weather trapped London's coal smoke near the groundThe weeks before the Great Smog had been unusually cold, with heavy snow in the region. London households were burning large amounts of coal to keep their homes warm, sending smoke upwards through thousands of chimneys. Normally, that smoke would gradually rise and disperse. The weather in early December prevented that from happening.An area of high pressure had settled over the region, producing what is known as a temperature inversion. Instead of becoming cooler with height, the air above the surface was warmer. The colder air remained close to the ground, effectively holding smoke and other pollutants beneath it.There was little wind to break up the stagnant layer. Pollution from London's homes and factories accumulated alongside material carried into the capital from industrial areas on the continent. The morning of 5 December began with clear skies, light winds and moist air near the ground. As the surface cooled, the moisture condensed into fog. Beneath the temperature inversion, that fog became mixed with the smoke coming from London's chimneys.London's Great Smog turned streets into a mazeThe fog was not especially dense during the daytime on 5 December. After darkness fell, however, conditions deteriorated rapidly. Visibility in some places dropped to only a few metres. The following day, the low winter sun was not strong enough to disperse the fog, and it thickened again after nightfall. The same pattern continued into Sunday and Monday. For people walking through London, even streets they knew well became difficult to negotiate. In the Isle of Dogs, the fog was reportedly so dense that people could not see their own feet.The disruption reached far beyond pedestrians. Travel was badly affected for several days, while the polluted air caused breathing difficulties among many people. The quantities of pollution released during the episode were considerable. Each day, around 1,000 tonnes of smoke particles entered the atmosphere, along with 2,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide, 140 tonnes of hydrochloric acid and 14 tonnes of fluorine compounds.The Met Office reported, sulphur dioxide was also present in large quantities. Around 370 tonnes were released during each day of the fog, with an estimated 800 tonnes of sulphuric acid ultimately formed from it.Thousands died after the Great Smog finally clearedThe Great Smog finally lifted on 9 December. Its effects did not end with the return of clearer skies. About 4,000 deaths were initially attributed to the episode. The eventual death toll was found to be much higher as the longer-term consequences became clearer. Many people developed serious respiratory problems during and after the smog.There were also contemporary reports of livestock being affected. Press reports claimed that cattle at Smithfield had been asphyxiated by the polluted air, although the circumstances surrounding those reports were not as firmly established as the wider evidence of the smog's effect on human health.Four years later, Britain began tackling its deadly coal smokeThe response was not immediate, but the Great Smog helped push air pollution higher up the political agenda. The Clean Air Act of 1956 introduced measures intended to reduce the amount of smoke released into Britain's towns and cities. Among other changes, it restricted the emission of black smoke and encouraged the use of smokeless fuels. Urban households and industrial operators were given time to adjust to the new requirements rather than being forced to change their heating and production methods overnight. The legislation marked an important change in Britain's approach to coal smoke. The familiar urban fogs did not disappear immediately, though.Smoky fogs were still occurring after the 1956 Act. In 1962, another London fog was associated with around 750 deaths. The number was devastating, but the episode was nowhere near the scale of what had happened a decade earlier. A further Clean Air Act followed in 1968, extending the restrictions on smoke and helping to continue the shift away from the conditions that had produced London's notorious smog.How clean air laws helped clear London's coal-filled fogsThe Great Smog became a turning point in the history of British air pollution. London's famous dirty fogs had been developing for more than a century, shaped by industrialisation, widespread coal burning and the city's particular geography.The 1952 episode showed what could happen when those ingredients were combined with stagnant weather. The subsequent clean-air laws, together with changes in domestic heating and other developments, gradually removed many of the conditions that had allowed such severe pollution to build up over the capital.You use AI every day.
